Article Title: 'Congress spreading anarchy': BJP draws parallel between France and Delhi protests
Article Text:
BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia on Thursday questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with foreign-based organisations, including Progressive International and Indian Alliance Paris, accusing them of amplifying protests in India and alleging a wider conspiracy to create “anarchy and chaos” in the country.Addressing a press conference, Bhatia repeatedly referred to Gandhi as “Rahul Gaddar” and alleged that the Congress leadership’s engagement with international groups raised questions about their activities, funding and possible coordination with protests in India. His remarks followed a Fox News Digital investigation that claimed to have identified 101 organisations across nine countries involved in organising, coordinating or amplifying demonstrations.“This Progressive International organisation describes itself as a transnational anti-capitalist organisation. According to the report I showed, the unrest and vandalism of historical monuments in France, the incidents in Spain, what is happening in India, and the events in Albania are all linked to Progressive International", Bhatia claimed, alleging that the events formed part of a coordinated effort to challenge elected governments and constitutional institutions.“The subject is the model of anarchy, chaos, and treachery that the Leader of the Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, is presenting before the country. Now, a news report was published in a very prestigious newspaper today, regarding how these threads of treachery are connecting with foreign agencies,” Bhatia said.“If it is asked, who is the commander-in-chief of this traitor? Who is the leader of this traitor? Then it would not be wrong,” he added.Bhatia cited the report’s references to Indian Alliance Paris, a France-based organisation, alleging that it was among the first to share videos and amplify social media posts concerning Gandhi’s detention during a protest. He questioned whether the organisation’s activities indicated an attempt by foreign-based groups to influence the narrative around India’s domestic political affairs.“This Progressive International organisation describes itself as a transnational anti-capitalist organisation. According to the report I showed, the unrest and vandalism of historical monuments in France, the incidents in Spain, what is happening in India, and the events in Albania are all linked to Progressive International", Bhatia claimed, alleging that the events formed part of a coordinated effort to challenge elected governments and constitutional institutions.“Wherever there is an elected government, they want to overthrow it. They want to destroy constitutional institutions such as the Supreme Court and Parliament, as well as historical buildings..,France, Albania, Spain and Delhi protests — everything is linked", He claimed, referring to a Congress social media post documenting a meeting between Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and a delegation from the organisation at 10 Janpath in New Delhi in April, 2025.“Rahul Gandhi... Rahul the ‘Gaddar’? Does he not have any strength left in him anymore, that now he has to take the help of such agencies and organisations that are anti-India?” Bhatia said.“Both the names I gave you—Progressive International, with proof, is a meeting on Congress's handle,” he said, referring to the party’s post. He alleged that the organisations were connected to protests and unrest in France, Spain and Albania, and sought clarification from the Congress about the nature of its engagement with them.Bhatia also referred to a social media post by Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut about protests in Albania, alleging that it could be interpreted as support for actions against constitutional institutions. He linked this to slogans raised by protesters on the Supreme Court premises, which he claimed were part of a broader attempt to undermine democratic institutions.“Protesting is a fundamental right, but destruction, destroying institutions, arson, and violent demonstrations are not fundamental rights,” Bhatia said.He demanded that Rahul Gandhi and the Congress disclose what was discussed during the meeting with Progressive International, clarify whether any agreement had been reached and explain the sources of funding for the organisations, including whether they had links with foreign individuals or entities.The Fox News Digital report, titled Global Chaos Inc Grows to 101 Groups, also referred to an international coalition of 28 communist and socialist youth organisations allegedly mobilising students for coordinated strikes across Europe. It said the network extended to the US, UK, Greece, Brazil and India, with groups mobilising supporters, calling strikes and amplifying demonstrations through international media outlets.The report also cited the Neville Roy Singham network and Indian Alliance Paris as alleged amplifiers of French demonstrations on social media, drawing parallels with student protests in India. The claims of coordinated efforts to influence protests in India were not independently established by the material cited at the press conference.Bhatia also criticised Rahul Gandhi’s interactions with British MP Jeremy Corbyn and US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, alleging that their positions on Kashmir were contrary to India’s interests. He accused Rahul of seeking support from organisations he described as anti-India. "Such organisations may be anti-India, but how can the LoP of the country India be anti-India?", he asked.
Article Summary: Gaurav Bhatia questions Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with foreign-based organisations, including Progressive International and Indian Alliance Paris. He accuses them of amplifying protests in India and alleging a wider conspiracy to create “anarchy and chaos” in the country.

Article Title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka seek more time, skip Delhi Police questioning
Article Text:
Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will not appear before the Delhi Police Crime Branch for questioning on Thursday after seeking more time, sources told ANI. Police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, the sources said.The Crime Branch had summoned Das and Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday, a day after they were released from judicial custody.The two were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed them to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the enquiry. They were also instructed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.In their written undertakings, the leaders promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future demonstrations would be held within the constitutional framework.The two leaders were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. Police alleged that they entered the area through private premises and violated conditions related to maintaining peace.The Delhi Police had earlier sought a further three-day extension of their judicial custody, citing concerns over a possible breach of peace and law and order. Police also pointed to alleged differences between statements made by the leaders before the court and their subsequent remarks to the media.The matter is scheduled for further proceedings before the SEM court on October 23 at 3 pm. Das, Ranka and their sureties have been directed to remain present.
Article Summary: Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office. Police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, the sources said. The two were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds.

Article Title: 'They have the right to protest, argue': Ex-BJP leader Annamalai questions govt's handling of CJP protests
Article Text:
‘I disagree with CJP’s protest strategies’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has questioned the Centre over its handling of protests by the CJP group in Delhi, raising concerns over restrictions at Jantar Mantar, preventive detention and bail proceedings involving its office-bearers.In a series of posts, former BJP leader K Annamalai invoked then-Gujarat CM Narendra Modi’s 2011 remarks condemning the police crackdown on an anti-corruption protest at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, questioning whether the principles Modi defended then applied to protesters today.“In 2011, the then Gujarat chief minister, Narendra Modi, said that if his hands had not been tied, he would have gone to Delhi and revolted against the central government,” Annamalai wrote.“In my view, what the honourable Prime Minister Narendra Modi said then was absolutely right. There was nothing wrong with it,” he added.Annamalai, who said he left the BJP on June 5, 2026, questioned how Jantar Mantar was removed as a designated protest site after CJP sought permission to hold a demonstration.He also raised concerns over an assistant commissioner of police (ACP) functioning as a special executive magistrate with the authority to decide whether a person should remain in preventive detention.“In the CJP case, Delhi Police itself is the complainant, while an ACP belonging to the same Delhi Police force has the authority to decide whether the accused should remain in preventive detention,” he said.He also questioned why eight bail sureties had been rejected and why a magistrate had cross-examined a person offering bail surety. Annamalai further asked whether action had been taken over the alleged use of pellet guns and other standard operating procedure violations during protests against the NEET examination.Comparing the situation with protests during previous Congress and Aam Aadmi Party governments in Delhi, he asked how BJP workers who allegedly jumped barricades or disobeyed police orders had been treated.“Was it anything like what is happening now? Certainly not!” he said.Annamalai said he disagreed with CJP’s approach but defended its right to protest.“As I said yesterday, I do not agree with CJP’s protest strategies, and I believe many of its approaches are misguided,” he said.“But if you ask me whether they have the right to protest, argue and fight for an issue they consider important, my answer is an unequivocal yes!” he added.He also criticised the tendency to portray protests against the Union government as anti-national or foreign-funded.“It is genuinely exhausting and frustrating to see every protest against the central government and every statement it issues being portrayed as an anti-national act funded by foreign powers,” he said.Annamalai further questioned whether the BJP was inadvertently giving CJP publicity by targeting it, referring to a Dussehra event led by BJP MLA Ashok Goyal.“Is the BJP genuinely opposed to CJP, or is it giving the organisation free publicity?” he asked.The remarks come days after CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were arrested over an alleged attempt to trespass at Jantar Mantar, which had been de-notified as a designated protest site. They were sent to Tihar Jail and later released after signing a bond.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has questioned the Centre over its handling of protests by the CJP group in Delhi. He has raised concerns over restrictions at Jantar Mantar, preventive detention and bail proceedings involving its office-bearers. He also questioned whether the BJP was inadvertently giving CJP publicity by targeting it.

NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk on Thursday described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a “beacon of hope” amid global uncertainty and said he was proud to call him a friend, while highlighting the absence of conflicts of interest between India and Poland as the two countries seek to strengthen their strategic partnership.Addressing a joint press conference with PM Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, Tusk said the two countries had held fruitful discussions on expanding bilateral cooperation and building on the strategic partnership established during Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.“We had a fruitful discussion with Prime Minister Modi about how Poland and India can develop and strengthen their strategic partnership. The decision to establish this partnership was made jointly during Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Warsaw in August 2024,” Tusk said.“The synergies between Poland and India are quite clear. We have no conflicts of interest and no historical issues that divide us. We are building our friendship on the basis of trust, shared values, and ideas such as non-violence,” he added.Tusk also drew a parallel between Poland’s Solidarity movement and India’s tradition of non-violence, saying the Polish movement had been inspired by such principles.Praising PM Modi’s role on the global stage, the Polish prime minister said India’s leadership offered hope at a time of geopolitical uncertainty and instability.“Someone like you, Prime Minister, leading a country as powerful as India, is a beacon of hope for all of us. I am very proud, truly proud, to be able to call myself your friend, Mr. Prime Minister,” Tusk said.He also pointed to the economic progress made by both countries over the past 35 years.“Over the past 35 years, both our countries have experienced unprecedented economic success and dynamic growth. Let me put it straightforwardly, without any doubts or hesitation: the world looks upon us with envy, at how India is developing and at Poland’s development,” he said.PM Modi said the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had expanded opportunities for economic cooperation between India and Poland, building on the momentum in bilateral relations over the past two years.“Our growing economic strength has created new opportunities for the India-Poland partnership. And the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement has made these opportunities even broader,” PM Modi said.The two leaders witnessed the exchange of key memoranda of understanding before addressing the joint press conference.Welcoming Tusk, PM Modi recalled his visit to Poland in 2024, when the two countries elevated their relationship to a strategic partnership.“During that visit, we elevated our relations to the level of a Strategic Partnership. Building on this strong foundation, our partnership has gained new momentum over the past two years,” Modi said.He also highlighted the historical ties between the two countries, describing their friendship as rooted in shared humanity and empathy rather than diplomatic relations alone.“The friendship between India and Poland is not based merely on diplomatic relations, but on the shared heritage of humanity and empathy,” Modi said.Recalling the assistance extended to Polish families during the Second World War, PM Modi said the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter to thousands of Polish children and families in India.The prime minister also said the two sides had agreed to strengthen cooperation in culture, education, sports and tourism. He added that they had discussed regional and global developments, democratic values and the need to reform global governance institutions.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace,” PM Modi said.Tusk arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for an official visit from October 21 to 23, at PM Modi’s invitation. He is accompanied by Poland’s minister of finance and economy Andrzej Domanski and a business delegation.The two prime ministers held delegation-level talks at Hyderabad House to review bilateral relations and explore cooperation across trade, defence, technology, space and other areas.India’s delegation included external affairs minister S Jaishankar, national security adviser Ajit Doval and foreign secretary Vikram Misri.Earlier on Thursday, Tusk paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat, laying a wreath at the memorial. Jaishankar also called on the Polish prime minister to discuss ways to deepen bilateral cooperation.In a post on X, Jaishankar said, “Pleased to call on Prime Minister Donald Tusk @donaldtuskof Poland. Appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India - Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains.”During his visit, Tusk is scheduled to attend the India-Poland Business Forum in New Delhi before travelling to Bengaluru on October 23 for engagements with leaders from India’s information technology and space sectors.Former Polish ambassador to India Adam Burakowski has said both countries aim to increase annual bilateral trade from approximately $6 billion to $10 billion.He has also identified defence and space technology as key areas for cooperation and pointed to the India-EU trade agreement as an opportunity to expand economic engagement.Tusk’s visit marks the first visit by a Polish prime minister to India since 2010. The two countries established their strategic partnership during PM Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.
Article Summary: Poland's PM Donald Tusk and Indian PM Narendra Modi held a joint press conference in New Delhi on Thursday. Tusk said the two countries had held fruitful discussions on expanding bilateral cooperation and building on the strategic partnership established during Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.

Article Title: 1 Indian killed, 2 injured in Dammam airport attack in Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
One Indian killed, two injured in attack on Dammam airport in Saudi Arabia

NEW DELHI: One Indian national was killed and two others were injured in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday night, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Thursday.Saudi authorities informed India that two people were killed in the attack, including one Indian national, the MEA said, adding that it was ascertaining further details and contacting the affected families.“Our thoughts and prayers are with the family and loved ones of the deceased and we wish speedy recovery of the injured,” the MEA said.Saudi Arabia's general authority of civil aviation (GACA) said the airport was targeted on Wednesday evening, October 21.The injured were taken to hospital for medical treatment, while the attack also caused property damage, the extent of which was being assessed, GACA said.Meanwhile, the US state department ordered the departure of non-emergency government employees and their family members from Saudi Arabia, citing security concerns.State department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said Iran-backed Houthis had increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure, resulting in civilian casualties and travel disruptions.
Article Summary: One Indian national was killed and two others were injured in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities informed India that two people were killed in the attack, including one Indian national. US state department ordered the departure of non-emergency government employees from Saudi Arabia, citing security concerns.

Article Title: 'You want to protect infiltrators' votes': Amit Shah's sharp attack on Rahul Gandhi over 'vote theft' claims

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday hit out at leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of “vote chori” and "collusion" between the Election Commission and the BJP , accusing the Congress of using the issue to explain its electoral defeats.Addressing an event in Delhi on his birthday where he launched projects worth Rs 8,941 crore for cleaning the Yamuna, Shah also targeted the Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over its governance in Delhi and Punjab.“The BJP keeps winning elections, and the opposition is troubled by it. That is why they have come up with the excuse of ‘vote chori’, or vote theft,” Shah said.“Rahul ji, you keep talking about vote theft because you want to protect the votes of infiltrators,” he added.Union home minister argued that the BJP had been winning elections in several states even before Narendra Modi became prime minister, while the Congress had remained out of power in many states for decades.“Congress, its allies accuse BJP of vote theft but are out of power in many states for decades,” he said.Referring to the Congress's electoral record, Shah cited its prolonged absence from power in several states and questioned whether its electoral setbacks had begun only after Modi became prime minister.“When I say the BJP will remain in power for 30 years, they accuse us of stealing votes. They ask how Amit Shah knows the election results in advance. Amit Shah was born here, lives here and will die here. I do not have to travel abroad every six months. I live among the people of this country,” he said.Attacking Lok Sabha LoP he said, "When court rulings favour you, you call them fair, but when they go against you, you question them. These double standards will not work, Rahul ji."Shah also targeted Rahul over opposition protests in Delhi, saying, “You cannot overturn the people's mandate through political manoeuvres and mob pressure. Winning elections is not about staging protests and sit-ins.”Shah also accused previous governments in Delhi of failing to prevent untreated sewage from entering the Yamuna and said the BJP government was committed to cleaning the river.“Congress, AAP govts allowed discharge of sewer water in Yamuna; we will clean it by May 2029,” Shah said.The projects launched at the event are aimed at improving sewage treatment and wastewater management, expanding sewer connections and reducing pollution in the river.Turning to poll-bound Punjab, where the AAP government is led by chief minister Bhagwant Mann, Shah attacked the ruling party over the drug menace and expressed confidence that the NDA would come to power in the state.“Drug menace prevalent in Punjab; people of state want NDA government,” he said.“AAP is going to be routed in Punjab elections , we will end drug trafficking in state,” Shah added.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah hit out at leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. He accused the Congress of using the issue to explain its electoral defeats. Shah also targeted the Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party over its governance in Delhi and Punjab.

Article Title: 'Told them to give it to me in writing': Raihan Vadra recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down at Bikaner House exhibition
Article Text:
Raihan Vadra alleges Bikaner House officials objected to protest photos, including those of Tricolour

Officials allegedly refused to provide written explanation

Dispute over photographs of the Tricolour

NEW DELHI: Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, has detailed his interactions with Bikaner House officials over the removal of photographs depicting youth protests in Delhi from his exhibition, alleging that the administration gave him only a few hours to comply with its objections.Speaking about the controversy, Raihan said his solo exhibition, titled No Idea Is Fine, was scheduled to open at 7 pm, but the venue's management raised objections to some of the photographs shortly before the event.He alleged that officials subsequently insisted that all 70 images be removed, including photographs featuring the Indian national flag.Speaking to news agency ANI, Raihan said the Bikaner House management first contacted him 24 hours before the scheduled opening and told him that some images violated its policy. He said he asked the officials to identify the photographs and discuss their objections, but did not receive a response until the following day.He said the deputy resident commissioner later contacted him and instructed him to remove the photographs, which documented youth movements in Delhi over the preceding year.“I said, 'I shared the layout a week earlier; why didn't you bring it up earlier?' They said, 'We couldn't see the layout.'So I said, 'You still had 1 week to tell me you couldn't see the layout. I would have sent it; we could have had the discussion earlier. Now, in 4-5 hours, what am I going to do?'” Raihan said.Raihan said he asked the management to provide written explanations for the removal of individual photographs but did not receive them.He said the principal resident commissioner subsequently visited the exhibition at around 3 pm and reiterated the objections. According to Raihan, the official cited the venue's policy against political content.Raihan said he had already removed most photographs featuring political parties and leaders and was willing to replace any remaining images that violated the policy.“For the most part, I had removed imagery of political parties and of political leaders. Maybe there were a few photographs; I said, 'We could discuss. If they are against your policy, I'll replace them.' He said, 'No, none of these 70 images will be put up,'” he said.According to Raihan, the management issued a notice at 3.30 pm warning that the building would be sealed and the exhibition cancelled if the photographs were not removed by 5 pm.He said he initially complied by turning the framed photographs around so that only their backs were visible. However, he alleged that officials objected to this arrangement as well, prompting him to take the frames down and move them into storage.Raihan said he left two photographs featuring the Indian flag on display, arguing that they could not reasonably violate the venue's policy. He alleged that officials asked him to remove them but did not provide a written order when he requested one.“I said, 'This can't be against your policy. How can it be against your policy?' I said, 'Give it to me in writing that you want me to take down a picture of the Indian flag.' They didn't,” he said.Raihan added that he left the venue to change clothes and that officials removed one of the two photographs themselves. One image of the national flag remained on display, he said.In an earlier statement, Raihan had said he would not remove the photographs featuring the Tricolour and that the exhibition would proceed in a limited capacity while he looked for an alternative venue to display the complete collection.The controversy drew reactions from members of the Congress. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son in a post on X, writing, “When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn’t know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. I am proud of you, always will be.”Robert Vadra also shared his son's statement, while Congress MP Karti Chidambaram criticised the Bikaner House administration's conduct.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera alleged that the removal of the photographs amounted to censorship.In a post on X, he said the works documented protests and questioned why images of demonstrations, including the national flag, had become objectionable.The exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, was scheduled to open at Bikaner House on Thursday evening.
Article Summary: Raihan Vadra alleges Bikaner House officials objected to protest photos, including those of the Tricolour.Officials allegedly refused to provide written explanation for the removal of the images. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son in a post on X.

Article Title: 'Tricolor row': What happened at Priyanka Gandhi’s son Raihan’s exhibition at Bikaner House - controversy explained

Why were the photographs removed

Priyanka Gandhi, Congress leaders react

NEW DELHI: A controversy erupted at Delhi’s Bikaner House after artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the venue’s management asked him to remove around 74 photographs documenting recent youth protests ahead of his solo exhibition, “No Idea Is Final”.Raihan also alleged that he was asked to remove two photographs of the Indian flag, saying he had refused to take them down.The exhibition opened as scheduled on Wednesday, with around 40 photographs remaining on display while more than 70 were removed, according to a PTI report. The show, featuring wildlife photography, abstract works and images of recent youth movements, is scheduled to continue until Sunday.In a post on Instagram, Raihan wrote, "Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show "No Idea Is Final", which opens this evening at 7 pm. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently, the content is "objectionable". They also directed me to remove two photos of the Tiranga. I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag."Raihan told PTI that the management had raised objections to the “political nature” of the protest photographs. He said he was informed at 3.30 pm on Wednesday that the images had to be removed by 5 pm or the exhibition would be cancelled.According to Raihan, the management said that, given the prevailing political climate in India, it was not the right time to display the images. He maintained that the photographs did not convey a political message and merely documented protests over the preceding six months."I felt it is my duty as an Indian artist, not just because I am doing a show right now, but it is my duty as an Indian artist to document what is going on... They are censoring the work of artists, I don't know what they are scared of. They even went to the extent of removing the picture of the Indian flag," he told PTI.Raihan also said he had shared the exhibition proposal and layout with the management well in advance and objected to the removal of nearly half the artworks less than 24 hours before the opening.A Bikaner House official told PTI that the administration was not authorised to comment on the matter.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra criticised the alleged removal of the photographs, describing it as an attempt to silence young voices."I think it's ridiculous. What do you think? He is a young boy but I suppose you know, they are muzzling the voice of the youth across the nation. So it's only expected that they'll do it to anyone," she told PTI."His photographs of the protests, not a single commentary, not a single thing that was either derogatory towards anyone, just a visual documentation of the protest. So, I mean, clearly this is the way they think. It's not a democracy anymore. Today it's him, tomorrow it'll be another artist," she added.Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera also criticised the alleged censorship, questioning why photographs documenting protests had been considered objectionable."When even the Tricolour isn’t safe from the censor’s scissors, perhaps the problem isn’t the art. It’s the regime. Just hours before @raihanrvadra was to open his art show ‘No Idea Is Final ’, 74 artworks - nearly half the exhibition - were taken down for being 'political ' by the Bikaner House. The photographs merely documented protests, and not one was derogatory or inflammatory. So what exactly was the offence?" he said.Khera further alleged that a photograph of the Tricolour was among the works Raihan had to fight to retain. Congress MP Karti Chidambaram also condemned the alleged censorship, calling the administration's behaviour "obtuse" and "churlish."The Indian Youth Congress Legal Cell also reacted to the controversy, posting on X: "IYC Legal Cell's tweet: YOU CAN CENSOR THE FRAME. NOT THE TRUTH. Saheb dara hua hai (sir is scared)."Raihan said the exhibition would continue with the works still on display and indicated that he could seek another venue if necessary to show the full collection of protest photographs.
Article Summary: Photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi, says he was asked to remove 74 photographs of recent youth protests. He claims he was told the images had to be removed by 5 pm or the exhibition would be cancelled. The exhibition opened as scheduled on Wednesday with around 40 photographs remaining on display while more than 70 were removed.

Article Title: ‘Anti-Indian hate is exploding’: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi flags rising anti-Hindu hate online

US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi on Wednesday (local time) raised concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti-South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social media, accusing major technology companies of profiting from online hostility and calling on Congress to hold them accountable.In a post on X, Krishnamoorthi said, "Anti-Indian hate is exploding on social media, and Big Tech is profiting from it. These companies have no incentive to stop the hatred they help spread. Congress must hold them accountable."He alleged that social media platforms were failing to adequately monitor hateful content, citing an increase of more than 240 per cent in posts promoting anti-South Asian hate.In a video attached to the post, Krishnamoorthi said, "Big Tech is not policing their social media platforms where there's been an explosion of anti-South Asian, anti-Indian, anti-Hindu hate. I'll just give you one statistic: the number of X posts, posts on X or tweets, basically touting anti-South Asian hate has increased by more than 240 per cent over a very short period of time.""And, unfortunately, Big Tech is profiting off of this hate. They have no incentive right now to decrease it. And so we have to at this point, at the federal level, make sure that they face the full consequences of not taking action," he added.His remarks come amid growing concerns over online hostility towards South Asian communities and follow an attempted shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, on October 11.Krishnamoorthi was worshipping at the temple with his family when the alleged attack took place. He subsequently led 105 members of Congress, including every Indian American member of Congress, in urging FBI director Kash Patel to investigate the incident as a potential federal hate crime.According to prosecutors, 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis, a self-identified neo-Nazi, allegedly attempted to shoot a man outside the temple, but his rifle jammed. He fled the scene and later communicated plans to return. A coworker alerted the police, who arrested him that day.Prosecutors allege that Paporakis had authored an eight-page white supremacist manifesto describing violence against people of Indian descent at a Hindu place of worship.In their letter to Patel, the lawmakers wrote, "The alleged combination of targeted racial hatred, a religious setting, and preparations for mass violence demands a comprehensive federal response. We appreciate the FBI’s reported assistance to local investigators and urge the Bureau to ensure that potential hate-crime violations receive explicit attention."The lawmakers also sought details on whether the FBI was examining possible racial, ethnic and religious bias in the Aurora case, whether online platforms or other individuals had facilitated the alleged plot, and what measures the Bureau was taking to address credible threats against Indian Americans, Hindu Americans and other South Asian communities.The letter further stated, "We believe such messaging risks lending governmental legitimacy to racial and religious stereotyping. Federal agencies should make clear that debates over immigration or public safety never justify collective suspicion of Indian, Sikh, Hindu, or other South Asian communities."The lawmakers requested a written response to their questions by October 29, to the extent permitted by the ongoing investigation.Earlier, on October 20, Krishnamoorthi told news agency ANI that the US was becoming increasingly polarised, alleging that rhetoric from senior government officials was contributing to hostility towards minority communities."Well, yes, I do think that the America of today is more polarised than ever before," he said. He added that leaders at the highest levels of government were targeting groups, including Muslims, Indians and gay people, and "villainising people".Citing a controversial post by the department of homeland security targeting a Sikh man, Krishnamoorthi said, "I mean, the best example of that was the Department of Homeland Security tweet on their official account targeting a quote, unquote, 'Mr. Singh,' and saying, you know, 'self-deport or else. And predictably, one week later, a gentleman named Mr. Singh, a Sikh truck driver, was stabbed 17 times, came within inches of his life.The DHS post, which was later deleted, featured a Transformers-themed cartoon depicting an Indian Sikh man alongside the phrase "Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh” and the words “Self deport or find out".Calling for action against hate crimes, Krishnamoorthi said, "And this is what has to stop. If we're going to stop this horrible rash of hate, it has to stop at the top.""And once that happens, I think things become better, although we at all levels of government have to stand together against it," he added.
Article Summary: Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi raises concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti- South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social media. Alleges that social media platforms are failing to adequately monitor hateful content. Comes amid growing concerns over online hostility towards South Asian communities.

Article Title: Why are uninsured vehicles not part of crash relief scheme? Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: With Centre formulating a scheme to provide interim financial relief of Rs 2 lakh to families of road crash victims for deaths and Rs 1 lakh for grievous injuries, limited to accidents involving insured vehicles, SC has sought an explanation from govt on why it is not being extended to uninsured vehicles.Taking note that “Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026” has not been notified or publicised, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan directed the govt to publicise it to ensure awareness. People must be made aware of their right to seek interim compensation, it said.Union road transport ministry officials said the scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act. Govt informed SC that the ministry shared the scheme with states and UTs on Feb 23. SC had directed the ministry in April 2025 to formulate the scheme.On why it covers only insured vehicles, officials said it was framed under provisions of MV Act dealing with insured vehicles. If the offender’s vehicle is uninsured, the matter will go to a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT).The apex court bench examined clause 6 of the scheme, which specifies that victims or legal heirs of the deceased can apply through a designated online portal, providing details of claims filed or pending before a MACT.Officials said that Section 164 of the Act, which deals with compensation in cases of death or grievous injury, requires the vehicle owner or insurer to pay Rs 5 lakh and Rs 2.5 lakh for death and serious injury, respectively, under the “no-fault liability” provision. A claimant need not establish that death or injury resulted from wrongful act, neglect or default on the vehicle owner’s part.“Hence, interim relief was set at Rs 2 lakh for death and Rs 1 lakh for serious injury for immediate relief. Final compensation would be higher, depending on the order of MACT,” an official said.
Article Summary: SC has sought an explanation from govt on why it is not being extended to uninsured vehicles. Centre formulating scheme to provide interim financial relief of Rs 2 lakh to families of road crash victims for deaths and Rs 1 lakh for grievous injuries. Union road transport ministry officials said scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act.

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram on Thursday and shared the first look of her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which is scheduled for release on November 10.In her first post on the social media platform, the 79-year-old Congress leader expressed gratitude while introducing the book to readers.“Hello everyone, I’m truly grateful to share this moment with you all; the first look of Belonging: A Journey of Love,” she wrote in the caption.“It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” the post added.The memoir traces Congress MP’s journey from her childhood in post-war Italy to her relationship with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with India.The book recounts Sonia’s early years in Italy, her romance with Rajiv Gandhi while they were associated with Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband.Born in Italy, Sonia Gandhi was 19 when she met Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge, England, in 1965. The couple married on February 25, 1968.She went on to become the longest-serving president of the Congress party.Her memoir is expected to offer a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, alongside her experiences as a member of the Nehru-Gandhi family and her life in India.Rahul Gandhi had earlier expressed excitement about the book. On the 82nd birth anniversary of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha wrote that he was proud his mother’s story would reach readers.“I am happy, and so proud, that your story--'Belonging: A Journey of Love'--will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia,” Rahul Gandhi said.The memoir is scheduled to be published internationally by Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of the Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group, on November 10. The announcement was made on August 18.However, the book’s publication in India has faced uncertainty following a disagreement between Penguin Random House India (PRHI) and the author’s representatives over editorial changes.Penguin India said the publication process had reached an “impasse over a particular issue” during its normal editorial review. NEW DELHI: The shooters involved in the attack on actor Tiger Shroff received their weapons through a “dead drop” arrangement on Oct 17, just a day before the incident. Couriers Babita and Radha — who have since been arrested — were provided the weapons at New Delhi Railway Station by the main supplier, identified as Kunal.Kunal, who has also been arrested, has emerged as a key character who had been in touch with gangsters Anil Pandit and Randeep Malik for over two months. He had also figured as the source of the weapon used for the murder of a forex-hawala trader in Sonipat last year, sources said.In this case, he was relaying the instructions from Pandit to the two women after dropping them at the station on Oct 15. The women reached Mumbai on Oct 17, got off at Dadar and checked into a hotel. Around 11am, one of the shooters collected the bag with the weapons at an isolated spot near the hotel, an official added.The dead drop method — borrowed from spycraft — has increasingly surfaced in investigations involving terror modules, drug cartels and organised crime groups of late. Agencies have unearthed non-contact logistics where handlers use encrypted messaging to direct operatives to pre-arranged locations to collect weapons, funds and synthetic drugs.Some cases in point include IS-linked terror modules, cross-border drone-dropped payloads along the Punjab and J&K frontiers, interstate gang firearm procurements and synthetic drug delivery networks.Investigators reconstruct digital footprints, chat logs and GPS coordinates alongside CCTV footage analysis to establish the timeline. By using technical surveillance, cell tower dumps and financial intelligence tied to encrypted communications, agencies are able to intercept these isolated drop routines to cut off unverified supplier-courier links, sources said.
Article Summary: The shooters involved in the attack on actor Tiger Shroff received their weapons through a ‘dead drop’ arrangement on Oct 17, just a day before the incident. Couriers Babita and Radha were provided the weapons at New Delhi Railway Station by the main supplier.

Article Title: Confidence in poll process key for democracy, halt list of candidates: SC to AP SEC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday said instilling confidence in the election process was vital for democracy and the rule of law as it directed Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) not to declare the final candidate list for 19 of the 100 local bodies where opposition YSRCP has alleged that its candidates were prevented from filing nominations. However, the court refused to tinker with the Oct 28 polling date.An autumn-break bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and VMohana asked SEC to decide by Thursday if it should, after considering representations from candidates alleging use of force to prevent them from filing nominations, give additional time for filing of nominations or postpone polls. Accepting the suggestion of senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, SC asked DGP to give adequate security at nomination filing centres and to candidates.Senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, said in 19 of the 100 urban local bodies — 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities/nagar panchayats — more than 63% of YSRCP candidates were prevented from filing nominations or their nomination papers were torn. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, for AP govt, said YSRCP was importing criminal elements from as far as Punjab and fomenting violence only to cry wolf later.SEC, through senior advocate K Parameswar, denied YSRCP’s claims.The SC bench said, “Free and fair elections are a basic structure of the Constitution. Right to participate in such elections by filing nomination papers is a facet of the free and fair election process. It is the constitutional mandate to vest the SEC with the duty of conducting and supervising such elections which would necessarily include all steps to ensure free and transparent filing of nomination papers by contesting candidates. The power of constitutional courts in exercise of judicial review, though deferential to the conduct of elections by the EC, cannot be said to be only nugatory.”SC said it was the duty of SEC to direct the state law-enforcing machinery to provide adequate security and maintain law and order to provide candidates a secure environment to file their nomination papers in a peaceful manner.Referring to Singh’s allegations that the state police were, at times, indifferent or selective in registering complaints of YSRCP candidates, Parameswar said SEC had issued directions to police and Luthra said police had taken adequate measures to control law and order issues.Referring to the allegations of the principal opposition party, backed by prima facie material of violence unleashed to prevent filing of nominations, SC said, “We are conscious of judicial deference to the powers of control and superintendence of elections by EC. Such philosophy of deference has grown from a doctrine of necessity that the election process be entrusted in the hands of an independent constitutional authority and the process completed within a specified period and not get mired in the quagmire of judicial interference.“...It also cannot be ignored that the custody of constitutional values lies with constitutional courts and the power of judicial review to ensure fair and impartial elections cannot be wholly muted when the principal opposition political party in a state is before us and has placed on record representations and material expressing serious apprehensions with regard to hindrance in participation in election process through filing of nomination papers. ”

Last week, commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal had said that the deal had almost been finalised and what remained was the legal vetting, while stating that it will be implemented once there was clarity on India’s competitive advantage.However, officials in Delhi were parsing Trump’s statement about the likely deal being different, and keeping their fingers crossed given the many twists and turns during the negotiations.There has been speculation in certain quarters that the much-awaited deal may not be comprehensive, covering all sectors, and the two sides may like to leave aside the issues which have been particularly nettlesome to have an understanding on those for which they have been able to hammer out agreements.Last year, Indian oil companies entered into agreements to import gas from US, and there are demands from American companies on specific technological products, which govt is willing to accept, provided these help secure easier access for locally produced textiles, footwear and engineering goods.A comparative advantage for India — a reference to lower additional tariffs on exports from the country — will depend on how the Trump administration uses the powers under the Trade Act to impose duties on imports from across the world.Currently, Indian exports to US face 10% additional tariffs, under Section 301, for govt’s alleged failure to check the import of goods made using forced labour, with the administration arguing that the “unfair” advantage acts as a barrier for US exports. Additional tariffs of 10-12.5% have been imposed on over 50 countries.The outcome of a second probe under the same provision related to structural overcapacity is awaited. Officials here indicated that clarity was required on some of the aspects and the assessment is that things will be clearer after the US mid-term elections, slated for the first week of Nov, for which Republicans have made the Trump administration’s claim to have secured higher protection for American business and labour one of their key planks.In Aug 2025, Donald Trump imposed a 50% tariff on Indian goods, including a secondary tariff of 25% for Russian oil imports, which was withdrawn.

The magistrate took the undertakings on record, Live Law reported.After considering submissions from both sides and the written undertakings, the magistrate held that the immediate preventive measures under Section 135(3) of the BNSS could be secured by requiring the two leaders to execute bonds to maintain peace.Das and Ranka were also directed to furnish personal bonds and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the inquiry.The magistrate also directed them to appear before the court on every date of hearing and maintain peace and public tranquillity in accordance with the terms of their bonds and undertakings.

NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal on Wednesday defended himself over reprimanding singer Daler Mehndi on stage during an event, saying the artiste should not have performed if he was unwell.Speaking to news agency PTI, Uniyal said Mehndi was only lip-syncing during the event and that, as a public representative associated with the event's organising committee, he came under pressure from people who wanted the issue to be questioned."Daler Mehndi, being a big name, was invited to the Kunjapuri Fair. If he was unwell, he should not have come to perform," the minister said."We were asked to make full payment of Rs 35 lakh in advance to the artiste; hotels were also booked in advance. Article Title: Monsoon's gone, El Niño isn't: Why India's weather worries are far from over
Article Text:
What is El Niño and how does it affect India's weather?

Global impact of El Niño

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

El Niño is putting the world on alert, and India could be among the countries facing its next major weather test. After a monsoon marked by a 13 per cent rainfall deficit, attention is shifting to whether the climate phenomenon will bring a warmer winter, disrupt rainfall patterns and add to the pressure on agriculture.From Indonesia’s raging wildfires to an unusually active Pacific hurricane season, its effects are already emerging across the globe. Now, the question is what a strengthening El Niño could mean for India in the months ahead.According to the BBC, El Niño has been strengthening for several months and is already influencing weather patterns worldwide, with Indonesia experiencing its worst wildfire season since 2015, heightened hurricane activity in the eastern Pacific and reduced monsoon rainfall in India.The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned that the phenomenon could intensify further towards the end of 2026 and persist into 2027, raising concerns over its potential impact on temperatures, rainfall and extreme weather events across different regions.For India, the immediate concern is whether the strengthening El Niño will compound the effects of the deficient monsoon and influence winter temperatures, rainfall and agricultural conditions in the coming months.El Niño is a climate phenomenon characterised by unusually warm sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. It is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a natural climate pattern that influences atmospheric circulation, wind systems and rainfall distribution across the world.For India, El Niño is closely watched because it is generally associated with a higher risk of below-normal southwest monsoon rainfall.The warming of Pacific waters alters atmospheric circulation and can weaken conditions that support the Indian monsoon, increasing the possibility of prolonged dry spells and rainfall shortages.While central India received near-normal rainfall, eastern and northeastern India recorded a 26 per cent deficit, classified as an exceptional drought, while southern states received 24 per cent less rainfall than average, according to the BBC.A strengthening El Niño could contribute to warmer-than-normal conditions in parts of India, potentially increasing pressure on water resources and agriculture.The World Meteorological Organization (WMO), citing the South Asian Climate Outlook Forum, projected normal to above-normal maximum and minimum temperatures across much of South Asia during October–December 2026.Higher temperatures later in the winter could also threaten wheat yields if heat coincides with the grain-filling stage, although the impact will depend on actual weather conditions.However, conditions in January and February will depend on evolving climate patterns, including western disturbances.El Niño is expected to push temperatures higher across much of the world while shifting rainfall patterns, increasing the risks of drought, wildfires and flooding in different regions.In Southeast Asia, including Indonesia, hotter and drier conditions are raising wildfire and drought risks. In contrast, parts of East Africa could experience heavier rainfall and flooding, while drought risks remain a concern in other areas.El Niño is also influencing tropical storms. The eastern Pacific has experienced heightened hurricane activity, while stronger upper-level winds over the Atlantic have suppressed hurricane development.In South America, its effects vary, with drier conditions possible in parts of the Amazon and increased rainfall and flooding in some southern areas.
Article Summary: After a monsoon marked by a 13 per cent rainfall deficit, attention is shifting to whether the climate phenomenon will bring a warmer winter. The World Meteorological Organization has warned that the phenomenon could intensify further towards the end of 2026 and persist into 2027. The immediate concern is whether the strengthening El Niño will compound the effects of the deficient monsoon.

Article Title: New norms for DL: Driving tutorial pass mark may rise to 75%, select licence services to be free

NEW DELHI: Road transport ministry has proposed raising the pass mark for safe-driving tutorial assessment from 60% to 75% and waiving fees for specified driving-licence services availed through online Aadhaar authentication, along with charges for changes to licence particulars such as name and address.The proposed changes to driving licence rules are aimed at tightening assessment requirements and to ensure availing licence-related services without any hassle. The changes proposed in the draft notification to amend sections of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules published late Wednesday night also seek to streamline online driving licence services, specify acceptable identity and residence documents, and introduce time limits for processing applications to change licence particulars.Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes. The higher qualifying score of 70% is aimed at making the assessment more stringent. The draft also proposes a defined procedure for online applications to change driving licence particulars, including name and address. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject applications for changes within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.An application for an address change that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved.The proposed rules also specify documents that can be submitted as proof of identity, age and residence. These include Aadhaar, passport, voter identity card, recognised educational certificates and birth certificates, among other documents. Electricity and household gas bills not older than three months are among the proposed address-proof documents.LIC policy would no more be accepted as a proof.The draft also provides for a consolidated application form covering services such as licence renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the SARATHI portal wherever available.In another proposed change, a vehicle class would be deleted from a driving licence within seven days of an application to surrender it. However, applicants permanently surrendering a class would not be eligible to obtain a learner’s or driving licence for that class for one year.The draft notification invites objections and suggestions from stakeholders within 30 days of publication. The proposals will come into force after final notification.
Article Summary: Road transport ministry proposes raising the pass mark for safe-driving tutorial assessment from 60% to 75%. It also proposes waiving fees for specified driving- licence services availed through online Aadhaar authentication. The proposed changes to driving licence rules are aimed at tightening assessment requirements and to ensure availing licence-related services without hassle.

Article Title: ‘Then, you are not Gen Z?’ Delhi High Court’s light-hearted exchange with CJP leaders; Dipke reacts

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court had a light-hearted exchange during a hearing on Wednesday involving Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, with Justice Subramonium Prasad remarking that the two were not part of Generation Z after being told their ages.During the hearing, Justice Prasad asked advocate Abhik Chimni, appearing for the petitioners, how old the two leaders were. Chimni told the court that Das was 27 and Ranka was 32.“Then you are not Gen Z. What is Gen Z?” the court asked.After being informed that Generation Z generally refers to people born after 1997, the court reiterated, “Then you are not Gen Z.”The exchange took place while the high court was hearing the leaders’ challenge to an October 19 order by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) extending their judicial custody until October 21.The exchange also drew a reaction on social media, with CJP leader Abhijit Dipke posting an image of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and writing, “The only person who qualifies as GenZ.”During the hearing, the court questioned why the petitioners had approached it under Article 226 of the Constitution when an alternative remedy of revision could be available to challenge the magistrate’s order.“Your second incident. You are a person who has actually broken a bond.Your remedy actually lies in revision,” the court observed.The bench also questioned whether the authorities could insist on stricter surety conditions following an alleged second breach of a peace bond.“Once you have broken peace for the second time, are the authorities not entitled to insist upon everything?” the court asked.The court further noted that a challenge to the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site was pending before the Supreme Court and that the notification had not been stayed. It questioned the petitioners’ decision to return to the site in those circumstances.The bench also expressed concern that breaking barricades could encourage others to violate prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).“The two petitioners here are at the forefront. When you go and break a barricade, the chances of 10 or 20 more people in violation of 163 are very high,” the court observed.Advocate Chimni argued that the SEM's October 19 order extending the petitioners' custody was legally unsustainable. He contended that the magistrate lacked jurisdiction to extend their custody and alleged that preventive proceedings were being used arbitrarily.He also questioned the rejection of the sureties, arguing that two additional sureties were available but had not been called for consideration.According to his submissions, the magistrate's order referred to discrepancies in photographs and difficulties in verifying details relating to one of the petitioners.The court suggested that the petitioners await the outcome of proceedings before the SEM, which was scheduled to reconsider their sureties at 2 pm on Wednesday. Chimni, however, expressed apprehension that the sureties could again be rejected on fresh grounds, requiring the petitioners to approach the High Court again.The petitioners subsequently withdrew their plea. Justice Prasad permitted the withdrawal, and the High Court clarified that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.Additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma, along with advocate Ashish Dixit, appeared for the Delhi Police, while Chimni represented Das, Ranka and the other petitioners.

With inputs from Arvind Chauhan, Kaushik Pradhan, Nisha Nambiar, Alok K N Mishra, Abhay Singh, Saptarshi Banerjee, Ashok Pradhan, Kautilya Singh, Lisa Monteiro, Amarjeet Singh, Rashmi Drolia, Navjeeven Gopal, Manvir Saini, Sreerag P S, K Krishnachand, Jignesh Parmar and Kapil Dave

For booth-level officers in Goa, enrolling a voter no longer involves one particularly tedious search: tracing the elector or a parent in the electoral rolls of 2002. That requirement has gone from the current registration process. The papers needed to establish eligibility have not.In Dehradun, Vibhanshu Bhatt, the BLO for Ajabpur, says a wider choice of supporting documents has made it easier to answer voters’ questions. A retired govt employee, for instance, can now offer documents other than a pension letter to establish their status.“With voters now having more options, it has become easier for us to deal with public queries and concerns,” he said.Across several states, BLOs are returning to households, collecting documents to resolve notices issued during the special intensive revision (SIR), and helping eligible voters left out of the rolls apply for re-inclusion. Some are working with a wider range of evidence. Others are helping applicants through the regular registration process, without the additional declarations or links to old rolls required during SIR.The states are at different stages, with officers handling pending verification, fresh enrolment or preparations for special summary revision (SSR). Nor has every state relaxed its documentary requirements. What connects much of the fieldwork is a more active effort to reach voters and help them complete the process.In Delhi, voters served notices because their details contained discrepancies or could not be linked to the 2002 roll no longer have to routinely queue for physical hearings at electoral offices. BLOs visit their homes and collect supporting papers. Assistant electoral registration officers can dispose of cases without formal hearings where the verification is sufficient.For daily-wage earners, the earlier visits to election offices meant losing work. Minor spelling differences, such as Narendra and Narender, are now being corrected without extensive documentation, officials said.“Officials have been directed to facilitate eligible voters rather than reject cases over procedural difficulties. However, prescribed eligibility requirements and documents remain applicable and BLOs do see documents such as birth certificate, passport wherever applicable before submitting declaration forms recommending disposal of cases,” an official said.By October 16, around 25 lakh of Delhi’s 33 lakh SIR notices had been resolved, against around 4 lakh by September 29.In Maharashtra , the BLO mobile application now has an “Other/Equivalent” option. Added after a proposal from chief electoral officer S Chockalingam, it allows supporting evidence beyond the 13 categories originally prescribed to be submitted for scrutiny.The provision is intended to help, among others, homeless people, particularly vulnerable tribal groups and sex workers who may lack the specified papers. Electoral registration officers (EROs) and assistant EROs assess the relevance and validity of the evidence.The numbers are substantial. Maharashtra issued notices to about 1.22 crore electors: roughly 59.76 lakh whose records could not be mapped to the previous roll and 62.48 lakh over logical discrepancies.BLOs can collect documents during home visits and upload them on ECINET for scrutiny. Where the evidence resolves the discrepancy, a routine personal hearing is no longer necessary. Further hearings can still be held when verification requires them.In Ahmedabad, engineering student Krisha Patel found that enrolling as a new voter required fewer papers than some of her friends had been asked to produce.“Unlike some of my friends who were asked to submit proof that their father or grandfather was a voter, I was asked to submit basic documents like Aadhaar card, birth certificate and photos.”Gujarat chief electoral officer Sandip Sagale said BLOs had been instructed to follow revised EC guidelines issued on Oct 15.“The documents establishing the relation of applicants to parents and grandparents are no longer mandatory according to the revised ECI guidelines. Registrations by first-time voters are very encouraging.”In Uttar Pradesh, chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa says current enrolment uses the regular statutory Form 6. Applicants no longer have to establish links with the 2003 rolls through their own names or those of parents or relatives.This is a return to the standard registration procedure after SIR, rather than a new nationwide concession. Rinwa said the original statutory Form 6 is being used during continuous updating of the rolls and will continue during SSR beginning Nov 12.Madhya Pradesh has also instructed district election officials not to seek a separate declaration with Form 6. Applicants must still provide the prescribed identity and address documents and make the form’s standard declaration that their information is true to the best of their knowledge.In Bengal’s current special enrolment drive, an official from the chief electoral officer’s office said applicants need not submit Annexure IV, the declaration used to establish family links with existing or previous rolls. BLOs continue to accept documents from the EC’s prescribed list.For Goa’s BLOs, removing the search through the 2002 roll eliminates a difficult step. But they say the documents for enrolment under Form 6 remain the same, whether someone is applying for the first time or seeking inclusion after deletion during SIR.For another set of BLOs, the immediate task is to return to names that did not make it onto the rolls.In Keralam, a drive that began on Oct 15 involves comparing pre- and post-SIR rolls to identify eligible voters omitted during revision. In Thiruvananthapuram’s Fort ward, BLO N Sajankumar is helping such voters seek inclusion. The exercise also involves checking information on deceased electors against local body databases maintained by the Information Keralam Mission.Chhattisgarh has supplied BLOs with booth-wise lists for a month-long drive to locate eligible omitted voters. They are making household visits, holding polling-station camps twice a week and organising separate camps at educational institutions for young voters.“BLOs are going door to door and, if a person earlier marked absent or shifted is now found, the Form 6 process is facilitated immediately,” a state govt official said. “But the documentary requirements have not been relaxed. The same standard documents applicable to an eligible voter continue to apply.”Completed applications and field-verification reports go to EROs for scrutiny. Finding a person at home does not, by itself, settle the application.In Ahmedabad’s Amraiwadi, special evening camps are scheduled from Oct 21 for night-shelter residents, labourers and homeless citizens, ahead of publication of the draft roll on Nov 12.Bihar is deploying 90,172 BLOs for a drive to enrol left-out voters and first-time applicants, with house-to-house searches and verification of records. The exercise is scheduled to finish by Nov 8.Odisha offers a measure of the additions already made. Since SIR, around 35,000 voters have been added to its rolls. Nearly 1,200 were eligible voters left out during revision; the remainder were newly enrolled voters. BLOs conducted door-to-door visits during a three-day drive from Oct 7 to 9, and registration continues till Oct 31.Delhi’s BLOs, meanwhile, have begun re-verifying 47.6 lakh people categorised as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate after they did not submit enumeration forms and were excluded from the draft rolls. Eligible voters found to have been wrongly excluded will need to apply through Form 6, with assistance from BLOs.In Jharkhand’s Khunti district, two tribal residents who lacked Aadhaar cards and conventional identity and address documents were enrolled after their eligibility was verified through land records, khatian documents and Gram Sabha testimony. Such evidence is subject to scrutiny by electoral registration officers, who decide applications on the basis of records available in each case.Chief electoral officer K Ravi Kumar has directed registration officers not to demand special or additional documents at SIR hearings and to consider available records where conventional proof is unavailable. Alternative verification has also been reported for vulnerable groups, including orphans, destitute women, residents of old-age homes and transgender persons.“Depending on the category, declarations, institutional certificates and field verification may be used,” Kumar said.BLOs can receive the evidence. EROs must examine it before deciding whether an applicant is eligible.In Dehradun’s Gandhigram, BLO Sarthak Srivastava said officers were finishing door-to-door checks of voters left off the roll, who now had more documentary options.In Goa, BLOs say residence proof remains a problem for tenants whose landlords refuse to give NOCs. Applicants must still furnish proof of residence, along with a birth certificate or school-leaving certificate.
Article Summary: BLOs can collect documents during home visits and upload them on ECINET for scrutiny. Applicants no longer have to establish links with their own names through the 2003 rolls. Minor spelling differences, such as Narendra and Narender, are now being corrected without extensive documentation.

Article Title: INDIA bloc huddle: Leaders to meet virtually on CEC row; SIR irregularities on agenda
Article Text:
INDIA bloc leaders to meet today to discuss strategy against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

Opposition steps up campaign against Election Commission

Kharge targets immunity law, EVMs

INDIA bloc challenges SIR, Jantar Mantar decision

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening to discuss their strategy over the ongoing row involving chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources cited by news agency ANI said, with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge set to chair the meeting.The meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand accountability from the Election Commission of India (ECI).The opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumar’s resignation.The Election Commission has maintained that it follows established procedures and defended its role in conducting elections.The INDIA bloc had earlier announced a joint action plan under its “Save Democracy” campaign. The proposed programme included protests, a march towards the Election Commission headquarters and a rally in New Delhi on November 1.On October 6, INDIA bloc MPs led by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi marched towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission’s headquarters, seeking a meeting with the poll panel.Delhi Police stopped the march amid heavy barricading and detained several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. They were later released.Following the protest, the ECI said Delhi Police had informed it that a delegation of around 240 MPs wanted to meet the Election Commissioners and submit a memorandum at the Parliament House Annexe.The poll panel described the proposed venue and manner of seeking the meeting as “unusual” under its established protocol.Delhi Police said the march had not been granted permission and cited prohibitory orders to explain its action against the protesters.The opposition subsequently approached President Droupadi Murmu. An INDIA bloc delegation, including Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party representatives, submitted a memorandum outlining its demands on October 9.The memorandum sought Kumar’s resignation, suspension of the SIR exercise, restoration of voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.The opposition also called for the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to the chief election commissioner and other election commissioners for official duties.On Wednesday, Kharge accused the BJP-led government of undermining democratic institutions and shielding election officials from accountability. He said the opposition’s campaign was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democracy rather than securing electoral gains for any particular party.Kharge criticised Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which grants legal immunity to current and former Election Commissioners for official duties.He argued that the provision protected election officials from accountability and demanded its repeal.“We are asking the BJP to repeal that law. Because you are giving protection to the Election Commissioner and letting him make mistakes. And whatever mistakes have happened today, they happened through Gyanesh Kumar. Why did you give him immunity? It was given so that you can make mistakes through him just by telling him to do so, and forgive him. The Chief Justice doesn’t have immunity. The President of India doesn’t have it. An Election Commissioner does,” Kharge said.He also called for Kumar’s removal, the scrapping of electronic voting machines (EVMs) and a return to paper ballots, while demanding stricter checks on changes to voter lists.“Follow the constitutional system, and remove Gyanesh Kumar, whom you have appointed today. Along with removing him, change the system too. Bring the previous law back, get rid of the EVMs, bring back ballot papers, and the software that sits in one place and controls the whole country. Stop using BLOs to make changes to the voter list,” he said.Kharge also criticised the government’s response to opposition concerns, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were using ministers and constitutional officials to avoid directly addressing the issues raised by the opposition.At a meeting on October 13, INDIA bloc leaders reiterated their resolve to continue the campaign and said they would challenge the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Kharge, have also approached the Supreme Court challenging aspects of the SIR exercise.On October 15, the Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission, Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on petitions challenging aspects of the revision exercise.The court also agreed to examine the denotification of Jantar Mantar and directed Delhi Police to preserve CCTV footage of the protests amid allegations of excessive force.Thursday’s meeting is expected to focus on the opposition’s strategy in the continuing dispute with the Election Commission, including its demands over the SIR exercise and accountability of the poll panel.
Article Summary: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening. Meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumar’s resignation.

Article Title: Kuwait-flagged tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz; all safe
Article Text:

Another tanker incident in Strait of Hormuz
