India reiterates call for safe maritime passage

NEW DELHI: A Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, with all crew members reported safe, Union minister of ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said.The vessel, M/T Al Dasma, was hit on October 21, amid the ongoing Middle East tensions.The minister said in a post on X that the authorities were monitoring the situation and were in contact with the ship management company to ensure the safety of the crew."On Oct 21, Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker M/T AL DASMA, carrying 21 Indian seafarers, was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. All 21 of our Indian crew members, along with the rest of the crew are completely safe," Sonowal said."We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and wellbeing of our seafarers," he added.The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) tracked the incident at a location 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman.According to Times Kuwait, the strike triggered a fire aboard the tanker, which was subsequently extinguished.The vessel remained stationary following the incident, and all crew members were reported safe.The latest incident comes amid a series of attacks and security incidents involving commercial shipping in the Gulf region.Earlier, on October 16, crude oil tanker MT ST 3, carrying 15 Indian seafarers, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. Sonowal had said that all Indian nationals aboard the vessel were safe and no casualties had been reported.In a separate incident on October 14, chemical tanker YARA J, carrying nine Indian seafarers, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage off Romania. Sonowal had said that all 24 Indian nationals aboard the two vessels involved in the incidents were safe, with no casualties or injuries.Other incidents have also raised concerns about the safety of Indian seafarers operating in the region.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) had earlier condemned attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on October 11.The ministry had referred to tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, which was reportedly struck by a drone at Sohar Anchorage.Nine crew members were rescued, while two remained missing. Another vessel, the Marshall Islands-flagged MT VALTHERA, was struck by an unidentified projectile, causing a fire on board.All 11 Indian seafarers aboard that vessel were reported safe.India has repeatedly expressed concern over attacks on commercial vessels and merchant mariners amid the escalating conflict in the Middle East.New Delhi has described attacks on commercial shipping as "legally and morally indefensible" and emphasised the need to protect seafarers and uphold freedom of navigation.The MEA has also called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure, while stressing the importance of ensuring the "safe and unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways".The government has said it remains in contact with ship management companies to monitor incidents involving Indian seafarers and ensure their security and well-being.
Article Summary: A Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. All crew members reported safe, Union minister of ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said. Incident comes amid a series of attacks and security incidents involving commercial shipping in the Gulf region.

Article Title: Rosatom completes supply of engineered safety features actuation systems for Kudankulam N-plant units 3 and 4
Article Text:
​Kudankulam N-plant​

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Russia state atomic energy corporation Rosatom’s division Rosatom Automated Control Systems has completed the supply of equipment for engineered safety features actuation system computerised subsystems (ESFAS CS) for units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu. The role of the general designer and supplier of equipment in the project belongs to Atomstroyexport.In total, about 300 items of equipment were manufactured and delivered to the plant – four sets of ESFAS CS in accordance with the number of safety instrumentation and control trains, per each power unit featuring VVER-1000 reactors.ESFAS is the system that monitors the process parameters of a power unit when there is a deviation from normal operation conditions. In case of an accident, the system automatically initiates the start of safety instrumentation and control systems and sends commands to actuators (boron injection pumps and other active protection means) in order to prevent a beyond-design-basis accident and bring the reactor plant to a safe state. The system also ensures reactor cooldown, which is a controlled decrease of coolant temperature and pressure down to safe values after the shutdown.To avoid simultaneous failure, they are physically separated — located in different rooms — and have autonomous power supply from separate diesel generators.Specialists developing the ESFAS CS for units 3 and 4 relied on the operating experience of the same system at Kudankulam NPP units 1 and 2, which allowed them to implement a number of optimised solutions. One of such solutions is the application of non-programmable modules that process signals from sensors without the use of microprocessors. This helps to reduce the dependence of safety functions on application software and increases the resistance of equipment to potential common cause failures.The final delivery of ESFAS CS equipment was yet another step of equipping the power units with Russian automation, control and safety systems, implemented through industrial cooperation. Installation on the site will be followed by the pre-commissioning stage, which includes the off-line and integrated tests of the systems.Following the tests, the systems will be prepared for commissioning and further operation at units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam plant.Kudankulam plant features six power units with VVER-1000 reactors, with the total installed capacity of 6,000 MW. The first phase (units 1 and 2) was commissioned in 2013 and 2017, respectively. The second phase (Units 3 and 4) is under construction.
Article Summary: Rosatom has completed the supply of equipment for engineered safety features actuation system computerised subsystems (ESFAS CS) for units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu. ESFAS is the system that monitors the process parameters of a power unit when there is a deviation from normal operation conditions.

Article Title: SC stays probe against Vijayan & kin for a week to enable him to move high court
Article Text:
SC clarified that its observations did not touch upon the merits of the case against Keralam ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday stayed for a week Kerala Police’s investigation against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case and said a division bench of HC should not have refused them permission to appeal against the single judge’s order directing an FIR and probe.A special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing appeals filed by Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law Mohd Riyas PA, stayed the probe by state police.Referring to Section 175(4) of BNSS, which requires a report from the public servant’s superior officer before ordering an investigation into a complaint against the public servant for acts done in discharge of official duties, the bench said, “The single judge not only directed registration of FIR, which is the mandate in SC ruling in Vijay Madanlal case, but ordered commencement of investigation and submission of final report. ”“Commencement of investigation and taking the same to logical conclusion will require due compliance with other statutory requirements under the special law (as laid down in Charanjit Singh judgement of Supreme Court),” it said.“These facts clearly make out a prima facie case of locus standi for the petitioners to seek leave to appeal against (single judge’s) order. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned order and permit the petitioners to pursue their appeals before the division bench of the HC,” it added.SC clarified that its observations did not touch upon the merits of the case. “The investigation into FIR shall remain stayed for seven days,” it said.On an ECIR registered by ED on the basis of the FIR lodged by Kerala Police, the bench said it was not expressing any opinion on its validity.When Kerala govt undertook not to proceed with the probe till division bench decided the appeals, SC said, “Your client was so eager to investigate. We do not appreciate the state govt functioning like this.”On Sept 7, two years after registering an ECIR, ED shared information with state police regarding the alleged payoff case. State govt set up an SIT for a preliminary inquiry. On Oct 9, a single judge set aside the inquiry and directed filing of an FIR, lodged on Oct 12.Vijayan told SC the alleged payments were made between 2017 and 2020 by CMRL to Exalogic, in which he was never a shareholder, director or employee. He said he had no dealings with CMRL and claimed the allegations were examined and rejected at every level up to SC, which dismissed a petition over the issue in October 2025.
Article Summary: Supreme Court stays for a week Kerala Police’s investigation against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing appeals filed by Vijayan, his daughter and son-in-law, stayed the probe by state police.

Article Title: NMC denotifies medical education rules; annual disclosures risk lacking verification
Article Text:
Any action taken while the regulations were in force would not be affected.

Without evaluation, med colleges’ disclosure would just be unverified claims

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

National Medical Commission has denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023. With the denotification, all specific penalties against medical institutions that fail to comply with any of the statutory provisions and regulations or minimum standards are no longer applicable.Any action taken while the regulations were in force would not be affected. However, NMC has not taken any action against many colleges flouting regulations as in the case of non-payment of stipend to MBBS interns and doctors doing PG. Colleges will now have little to fear if they do not pay stipend as the penalty for is not specified in the NMC Act.The Act only states that the Medical Assessment and Rating Board shall take such measures, including issuing warning, imposition of monetary penalty, reducing intake or stoppage of admissions or recommendation for withdrawal of recognition against a medical institution for failure to maintain the minimum essential standards specified.“Notwithstanding such denotification, the requirement of furnishing the annual disclosure report shall continue to operate” in accordance with relevant sections of NMC Act 2019, read the denotification announcement gazetted on Oct 14. NMC Act stipulates that the UnderGraduate Medical Education Board and the Post-Graduate Medical Education Board shall specify norms for compulsory annual disclosures by medical institutions.The 2019 Act also states that MARB may conduct evaluation of any institute at any time without prior notice. However, with the denotification, the aspects that need to be included in the evaluation report, such as verification of physical infrastructure, availability of the required number of faculty and review of feedback from students, have also been removed.Without evaluation by MARB, the mandated annual disclosure would just be claims by a medical college unverified by an independent assessment.
Article Summary: National Medical Commission has denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023. With the denotification, all specific penalties against medical institutions that fail to comply with any of the statutory provisions and regulations are no longer applicable. NMC has not taken any action against many colleges flouting regulations.

Article Title: Who are the terrorists? J&K and Ladakh high court questions ‘vague’ detention order
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: J&K and Ladakh HC has summoned the Srinagar deputy commissioner for a personal appearance over a “vague” preventive detention order under Public Safety Act that accused a 28-year-old man of supporting “aforementioned terrorists” without identifying a single one, prompting the court to question whether the officer had independently assessed the case or merely reproduced a police dossier.A single bench of Justice Wasim Nargal said preventive detention, which allows authorities to deprive a person of liberty without a regular criminal trial, demands the “highest degree of constitutional responsibility and procedural diligence”.“The safeguards embodied in Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution of India are not empty formalities,” the court said, adding that the detaining authority must independently assess the material and satisfy itself that legal conditions for detention are met.The court directed the DC to appear with the detention order, police dossier, material placed before him and records showing his consideration of the case and subjective satisfaction before ordering detention under PSA.HC was hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Zubair Amin Bangroo of Srinagar, challenging his detention under an order dated Jan 13, 2026. His counsel Nida Nazir said the allegations were vague, no FIR had been registered against him and the detention order appeared to have been passed hurriedly.The order accused Bangroo of developing close links with terrorists, supporting them logistically and morally, and allowing his home and other safe locations to be used as hideouts. However, Nazir said it neither identified the terrorists nor named the network or associates with whom Bangroo was allegedly in contact.HC found that the detention grounds referred to “aforementioned terrorists” without any preceding reference identifying a terrorist. The phrase raised a compelling question about whether the DC had independently formulated the grounds or simply reproduced the police dossier, the court said.“Personal liberty occupies a position of paramount importance in the constitutional scheme. Its deprivation, even for a single day, constitutes an injury which cannot subsequently be undone by the mere restoration of liberty,” the court said.
Article Summary: HC was hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Zubair Amin Bangroo of Srinagar, challenging his detention under an order dated Jan 13, 2026. His counsel Nida Nazir said the allegations were vague, no FIR had been registered against him and the detention order appeared to have been passed hurriedly.
